# Our tools

## R

We do the vast majority of our analytical work using the R programming language.

We are big fans of the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/) packages, as well as the fantastic [PHEindicatormethods](https://github.com/ukhsa-collaboration/PHEindicatormethods) package originally developed by Public Health England and now maintained by OHID.

## SQL

We use SQL for querying electronic health record datasets that we have access to, including:

* The East London Database, provided by the Clinical Effectiveness Group at Queen Mary, University of London
* The PHM Linked Data, provided by North East London Integrated Care Board

## git and GitHub

We use git for version control, particularly for collaborative coding projects. Our remotes are hosted on GitHub.

We use GitHub for project management, issue tracking, and code review.
